intro.title: Up and running in five minutes
intro.body: Pick the path that matches your environment. Docker is the recommended one. Once BamDude is up, the first browser visit walks you through admin setup.

requirements.title: Before you start
items: A Bambu Lab printer with **Developer Mode** + **LAN-Only Mode** enabled (Settings → Network).
The printer's **IP address** and **Access Code** (Settings → Network and Settings → Information).
A Linux box, Raspberry Pi, NAS, or any Docker-capable host on the same network as the printer.
Optional: a Telegram bot token from [@BotFather](https://t.me/BotFather) if you want bot integration from day one.

steps.title: Run with Docker
steps.subtitle: The fastest path. Single container, SQLite by default, persistent volumes.
steps.command:
docker run -d \
  --name bamdude \
  --network host \
  -e TZ=Europe/Kyiv \
  -v bamdude_data:/app/data \
  -v bamdude_logs:/app/logs \
  --restart unless-stopped \
  kainpl/bamdude:latest
notes: **`--network host`** makes printer SSDP auto-discovery work; on macOS / Windows Docker Desktop swap it for `-p 8000:8000` and add printers manually by IP.
Two volumes: `bamdude_data` (SQLite + 3MFs + thumbnails) and `bamdude_logs`. Keep them - they hold every print you've ever done.

steps.title: Docker Compose (from source)
steps.subtitle: Build the image yourself, easier to extend.
steps.command:
git clone https://github.com/kainpl/bamdude.git
cd bamdude
docker compose up -d --build
notes: Uses the `docker-compose.yml` shipped in the repo. Edit it to add Postgres, MQTT, or Spoolman as siblings.
Subsequent rebuilds: `docker compose pull && docker compose up -d --build`.

steps.title: Windows installer (.exe)
steps.subtitle: No Python or Node — one self-contained setup for Windows.
steps.body: Download **bamdude-windows-setup.exe** from the [Releases page](https://github.com/kainpl/bamdude/releases) and run it. It bundles an embedded Python, the pre-built frontend and ffmpeg, installs to `C:\Program Files\BamDude`, keeps your data and logs in `C:\ProgramData\BamDude`, and registers BamDude as a Windows Service that serves http://localhost:8000 on boot. A Start Menu shortcut opens the web UI.
notes: To update, download the newer installer and re-run it — your data, settings and printers are preserved.

steps.title: Manual install (Python venv)
steps.subtitle: For developers or environments where Docker is not an option.
steps.command:
git clone https://github.com/kainpl/bamdude.git
cd bamdude
python3 -m venv venv && source venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
uvicorn backend.app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000
notes: Python 3.12+ (only for this manual route — Docker and the Windows installer bundle their own).
For the frontend: `cd frontend && npm install && npm run dev` in a second terminal.

steps.title: First login + admin setup
steps.subtitle: Open the web UI and create the initial admin.
steps.body: Browse to **http://localhost:8000** (or the host IP). The setup gate refuses every API call except `/auth/setup` until the first admin exists - pick a username, set a password (≥8 chars, upper + lower + digit), and you're in. After that the login form takes over and the gate disengages forever.
notes: Forgot the admin password? `python -m backend.app.cli reset_admin` clears the setup flags so the next boot re-enters this flow.
Behind a reverse proxy? Set `TRUSTED_PROXY_IPS` so rate-limit and refresh-cookie code can read `X-Forwarded-Proto` correctly.

steps.title: Add your first printer
steps.subtitle: Auto-discovery via SSDP or paste the IP.
steps.body: Settings → Printers → Add Printer. SSDP picks up Bambu printers on the same subnet automatically; otherwise paste the IP. Then enter the **access code** (printer screen → Settings → Information). Hit Save - BamDude opens the MQTT/FTPS connection and the dashboard starts streaming live status.

steps.title: Optional: Telegram bot
steps.subtitle: Control the farm from chat.
steps.body: Create a bot via [@BotFather](https://t.me/BotFather) and copy the token. Settings → Notifications → New Telegram provider → paste the token. Enable Registration Mode, send `/start` to your bot. Settings → Telegram Chats → assign your chat a role (Operator works for most). The reply keyboard and inline menus are now wired up.
